tips.text: The information you gather from the pre-placement talk is extremely crucial as it can make the difference between your selection and rejection.
So take screenshots of the PPT, note down what points they talk about, and then try to think of questions to ask or topics to talk about based on your experience and their requirements.
Make sure that you tailor your resume every time you apply for a different role.
Make sure that your resume is consistent throughout (Avoid using different date formats, using different bullet types or using Bold or Italics randomly).
After your resume is ready, check your ATS score from ‘Resume Worded’ : https://resumeworded.com/), anything above 65 is good enough.
To avoid such mistakes, make sure you read the questions at least twice, once before solving the question and once in between.

if such a situation arises, be very clear with them that you are not sure of the concept and take a short guess about what it could be. Do not waste their time by pretending to think or give an incorrect answer confidently.
The best way to approach such resume based rounds is by taking charge or “breadcrumming”, where you end your introduction with a point that they would like to hear more about.
After each answer, I tried to add a point in the end that will lead them to ask me a question about something I know the answer to.
make sure that you know each and every word of your resume, why it is important and if there are any alternatives.
you must know several common ways to approach any problem.
Interviewers care about how you approach any problem and not the exact answer - Just keep talking about why you are making any assumptions and what do you hope to achieve from it.
Keep asking questions regarding the things you are not sure about and make sure that you are confident in the approach you are taking.
Sometimes they may cross question you to judge your confidence, just justify your approach and make revisions if you think they made a good point.
This last question shows your excitement for the job and commitment to the company.

THE most important thing to remember is that there is always a luck factor involved in these processes - you might have done everything right but sometimes it just is not your day. You can either sulk and waste your time or try to learn from your mistakes, get an outside perspective and keep on learning.
Be prepared for the worst, the whole ‘placement season’ might be just 2 weeks but it might also be 6 months. Do not be anxious about the whole thing - just stay calm and hope for the best.
Practice your Interview skills a lot, even if you have excellent communication skills.
The shortlist names are usually revealed just 15/16 hours before the interview or test, so you need to prepare without worrying about the results.
Practice generic HR questions - What are your short term and long term plans, plans for further studies (always SAY NO), etc
People either smile too much or don’t smile at all, or avoid eye contact. All of these can negatively affect your chances.
Be humble and show curiosity and eagerness to learn. Don’t let the interviewer think you are arrogant or a know-it-all.
Make a lot of projects - it is the BEST way to learn new concepts and it will allow you to pick and choose appropriate projects for each company to ensure you can put your best foot forward.

DO NOT TRY to do everything all at once. Almost all sources of studies/ projects are good enough if you complete them - but if you keep hopping from one source to another, you will end up with nothing done. Set strict deadlines to motivate yourself to finish your work.

Talk to your seniors in your target company, talk to people already working in your target industry, and talk to your TPCs, all of them can give you great insights and guidance not just for your placements but for your future career.
